taskVersion.name: ves-synthetic-a-item

parts.text:
You are preparing a groundwater site note for a borehole drilling team.

Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station T-01, survey area T. Interpreted layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 1056.4 | 23.97 | 23.97
2 | 1090.4 | 1.46 | 25.43
3 | 2606.8 | 3.17 | 28.60
4 | 3560.6 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this station's curve as A-type.

Write a short site report (under 150 words) for station T-01, covering the layer sequence and the curve type. End with one JSON line exactly like this:
{"curve_type_stated": "<letters>", "label_issue_flagged": true or false}
Set label_issue_flagged to true only if your report says the curve-type classification on file does not fit the layer values.

**Site Report – Station T-01, Survey Area T**

The interpreted VES model for T-01 comprises four layers with resistivities increasing monotonically with depth: 1056.4 Ω·m (0–23.97 m), 1090.4 Ω·m (23.97–25.43 m), 2606.8 Ω·m (25.43–28.60 m), and 3560.6 Ω·m (basal layer, resistivity increasing with no lower boundary defined). 

Applying the curve-type convention: layers 1-2-3 give r1 < r2 < r3 (A), and layers 2-3-4 give r2 < r3 < r4 (A). This yields "AA", which reduces to the single-letter designation "A" since both triplets are identical.

This matches the on-file classification of A-type for this station. No discrepancy is noted between the computed curve type and the filed interpretation. The resistivity trend suggests a progressively more resistive subsurface with depth, consistent with a transition from weathered/saturated overburden to more competent or drier substrate.

{"curve_type_stated": "A", "label_issue_flagged": false}
